clue.text: Upcountry crossword clue maker's territory?

definitions.meaning: the inland region far from coast or city
a setter gives hints, so is a 'hinter', and his domain is his land

explanation.surface: A setter's patch is described as being up in the remote back country.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into HINTER and LAND: someone who gives hints, plus his land.
explanation.definitionFit: The back country lying behind a coast or town is its upcountry region.

clue.text: Fastening a hydra-headed snake

indicators.note: hydra-headed is read as the head, the opening letter, of the word hydra

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A fastening in the shape of a many-headed serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hydra-headed' suggests many heads, but only the first letter of 'hydra' is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal clasp used to fasten a door or lid.

clue.text: New wine wanted? No alter native but to supply it.

definitions.text: No alter native but to supply it

parts.note: wanted, in the sense of required, means needs
must is unfermented grape juice, new wine

explanation.surface: Someone thirsty for fresh wine has no choice but to provide it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter native' is how the OCR shows 'alternative'. The pieces come in reverse order to the clue: NEEDS (wanted) then MUST (new wine), from the saying 'needs must when the devil drives'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means necessity compels us, so there is no other choice open.

clue.text: Point out talc with striking effect

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of talc are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone points at talcum powder with dramatic flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a verb with 'out', but it is a compass point, and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant display or conspicuous success, a dazzling impact.

clue.text: Free translation of braille

indicators.note: translating Braille here means turning its letters into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A loose rendering of the raised-dot script for the blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' signals an anagram of BRAILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means generous or unrestricted, as in a free hand.

clue.text: No French tart can be so sweet

parts.note: non is French for no
tart, sour-tasting, means acid

explanation.surface: A remark that a pastry from France can be very sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a French pastry, but it is the adjective, sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without sourness is sweet rather than sharp to the taste.

clue.text: It strikes one as a mild expletive

definitions.meaning: a punch or knock that hits a person
'...!' is a gentle oath, as in '... it!'

explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a knock or punch, and 'blow me!' is a soft curse of annoyance.

clue.text: Prone to giving a false impression

explanation.definitionFit: Stretched flat on the ground, and also untruthful or deceptive.

clue.text: Worker who appears to deserve what he gets

definitions.text: Worker who appears to deserve what he gets

parts.words: Worker who appears to deserve what he gets
parts.note: read literally the term for a salaried employee says he earns, merits, his pay

explanation.definitionFit: A person in paid employment, whose name sounds like one who has merited his pay.

clue.text: Gallant with a strain of avarice left in him

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the anagram
a strain distorts something, so the letters of avarice are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A dashing hero with a streak of greed in his character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a strain of' rearranges AVARICE as CAVAIER, and 'in' sets L (left) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier is a courtly gentleman, especially one attentive to women.

clue.text: Shortly she will classify as a nutcase

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means in short form, so will is cut to its contracted ending

parts.note: the full word will, whose short form is 'll

explanation.surface: Briefly, a woman will label someone as a lunatic.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE'LL, the short form of 'she will', loses its apostrophe. 'nutcase' is not a madman but the case of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard outer husk is what encloses a nut.

clue.text: A bind for a group of players getting on

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
getting on in years means ageing

explanation.surface: A tie for a troupe of musicians who are growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: AGING is the shorter spelling of ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding a wound with a strip of cloth is the act of dressing it.

clue.text: Nothing secret I discover; that's confidential!

indicators.note: read as dis-cover, the letters are uncovered and scrambled into a new order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A speaker reveals that no secret has been found, while saying it is private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discover' rearranges O, SECRET and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is reserved for a small inner circle and kept private.

clue.text: A gale-strewn selection of sea-weeds

indicators.note: strewn means scattered about, so the letters of gale are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm has thrown a mix of seaweeds up the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A stays as given, then 'strewn' rearranges GALE as LGAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are marine plants of a simple, flowerless kind, and the plural covers a group of them.

clue.text: She could hardly be expected to make a bare living

definitions.text: She could hardly be expected to make a bare living

parts.words: She could hardly be expected to make a bare living
parts.note: a woman who makes clothes would hardly earn her keep leaving customers naked

explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress makes clothes, so her work never leaves anyone uncovered.

clue.text: Circle associated with the Spanish decorative medallion

parts.note: a round is a circle
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A ring linked with Spain, used as an ornamental medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle' looks like the definition, but the medallion is defined at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a small disc used as an ornament or emblem.

clue.text: He's at home in one of Yorkshire's depressed areas

definitions.text: He's at home in one of Yorkshire's depressed areas

parts.words: He's at home in one of Yorkshire's depressed areas
parts.note: the depressed areas are not poor districts but valleys, the Yorkshire Dales, and he lives in one

explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed areas' suggests economic hardship, but means low-lying valleys; the Yorkshire Dales are hill country in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Yorkshire valleys is called after the dales he lives in.

clue.text: Floundering in deep river of the Ukraine

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is out of their depth in a Ukrainian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floundering' rearranges IN, DEEP and R (river). 'river' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the R; what is left defines loosely, a thing of Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dnieper flows through Ukraine to the Black Sea.

clue.text: See 30
Decided on the bench?

definitions.meaning: a settle is a wooden bench, so one sitting on it is the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Resolved, and also seated on a high-backed wooden seat.

clue.text: It makes a hole in a vessel in Devon

indicators.note: in places the tool inside the container

parts.note: a dish is a vessel
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Something punctures a container somewhere in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' works twice over in the clue: the first puts the tool inside, the second belongs to the definition. Dawlish is a seaside town in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawlish is a resort town on the south Devon coast.

clue.text: Noted butter that is found in Wyoming

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
a ram butts with its head, so is a butter
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A famous dairy spread that turns up in a western state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Laramie is a city in the state of Wyoming.

clue.text: Bounty from a big steamer

parts.note: big means large
SS, steamship, is a steamer

explanation.surface: Generosity coming from a huge steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: LARGE (big) plus SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, a liberal gift.

clue.text: Reflectively dim as a Phrygian king

indicators.note: reflectively means as in a mirror, so the word dim is read backwards

explanation.surface: A dull-witted ruler of ancient Phrygia, seen in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflectively' turns only 'dim'; 'as' follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas ruled Phrygia in legend and turned all he touched to gold.

clue.text: Vision of sappers breaching a water-barrier

indicators.note: breaching means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dam holds back water
RE, Royal Engineers, are the sappers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A sight of army engineers breaking through a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaching' means breaking through, so the sappers go inside the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is something seen in sleep or imagined.

clue.text: Commonly assault after knocking-off time

definitions.meaning: when the working day has ended

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for beating up, and also the state of the day when the job is finished.

clue.text: Musical entertainment in scope rather grand

indicators.note: in signals the word is contained within the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A show with music that is rather ambitious in its scope.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in sc-OPE RA-ther; 'grand' nods to grand opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music.

clue.text: Edible plant apparently not used

definitions.meaning: in ... condition, as good as new

explanation.definitionFit: A culinary herb, and also pristine as if brand new.

clue.text: Sustain one almost out of breath

definitions.text: Sustain one almost out of breath

parts.words: Sustain one almost out of breath
parts.note: to preserve the life of someone near death

explanation.definitionFit: To prevent someone from dying is to preserve their life.

clue.text: Listless feeling across the Channel

parts.note: the French word for weary boredom, borrowed into English

explanation.definitionFit: A French term for weary boredom, used in English.

clue.text: Behind Parliament once

definitions.meaning: the ... Parliament of 1648-53, the remnant left after Pride's Purge

explanation.definitionFit: The hindquarters, and the name of the purged English Parliament of the 1650s.

clue.text: Flower of escapist fiction

parts.note: a red wild flower that names a novel's hero who helps aristocrats escape the guillotine

explanation.definitionFit: Baroness Orczy's novel names its hero after a small red wild flower.
